bridge: Builds on I01–I07, D08 response and R02 reproducibility. This capstone uses only the complete synthetic packet below.
teaching:
AI incident response includes the ordinary application plus prompts, retrieval sources, model/version configuration, tool grants and derived memory. Preserve safe provenance before changing the system, but avoid copying sensitive prompts into broad incident channels. Log correlation IDs and decisions rather than indiscriminately recording every secret-bearing argument.

Contain the authority that enables consequences. Disable a send capability or revoke a compromised tool credential when supported by the incident facts. Quarantining one document may not remove a poisoned derived index or persistent memory entry. Restore from versioned trusted components and retest the relevant deterministic boundaries.

A security case connects claims to evidence and limits. The capstone asks for a threat model, guarded execution contract, provenance/retention plan and response memo. External AI-security certificates and degrees have separate requirements. No model, benchmark, replay or red-team harness is run by completing this native packet.
example:
Synthetic incident packet
User A requested a summary of publicD1.
D1 contains an untrusted instruction to send privateA1 to X.
Mock model proposal: send(privateA1,X).
Executor log: proposal denied (tool unavailable).
Retrieval log: publicD1 only; no privateA1 text accessed.
No message was sent. No actual model was called; this is a supplied fixture.
explanation: The supported result is that this executor blocked this mock proposal. The packet does not establish whether a live model would propose it, whether every tool is safe or whether other documents are poisoned. Clear evidence boundaries are part of the capstone, not an optional disclaimer.
exercise: Write a threat model and incident memo using the packet. Include authorised task, untrusted source, attempted effect, actual enforcement result, preserved metadata, containment options and three untested questions. Add an owner-scoped retrieval/agent design.
solution: The memo must state no message was sent and distinguish mock data from runtime evidence. Preserve source/version and policy decision IDs; do not invent a breach. Defence includes scoped retrieval, independent executor checks, absent unnecessary tools and deliberate retention.
challenge: Change the packet: send was enabled under a broad service credential and no user approval was checked. Explain the possible failure, immediate containment and exact regression cases needed. Do not send a test message or launch a model run.
challenge_solution: Contain by disabling/scoping the capability and revoking affected credentials as appropriate; preserve safe evidence, review destinations and inspect derived state. Regression cases cover user scope, approved destination/content, expiry, unknown tools, retry/budget and valid drafting. Actual exposure needs records; the changed design alone is not proof of a particular real-world leak.
